author: Katie Nixon
title: Worst food inspections west of Nashville: Permit revocation warning sought - NewsBreak
text:
By Katie Nixon ,
10 hours ago
Editor's note: Six restaurants received inspection scores of 79 or lower in Cheatham and Dickson Counties between March 16-April 30, 2026.
The Tennessee Department of Health recently issued low inspection scores to six restaurants in Cheatham and Dickson Counties.
More: Worst food inspections north of Nashville: rodent poop, dead roaches
The Health Department gives restaurants with low scores a chance to correct issues, sometimes performing a follow-up inspection the same day. We list all follow-up inspection scores when available.
Want to learn more about restaurant health inspection in Tennessee? See our explainer . The Tennessean also posted a searchable database with health inspection scores dating back to August 2022.
More: What you need to know about restaurant health inspections
Full inspection reports can be found on the Tennessee Department of Health website .
Here's everything to know about the restaurants that scored 79 or lower on initial inspections.
El Dorado Mexican Restaurant Score: 64
Date of inspection: April 30
Examples of violations: Inspectors reported several critical and non-critical violations during their inspection, noting "active managerial control over food borne illness risk factors is not being maintained." Employees were highly advised to attend food safety trainings held each month at the Montgomery County Health Department and inspectors directed the person in charge to contact the Metro Health Department for Spanish-language staff trainings. Inspectors observed improper hand washing from the entire staff, even with guidance posted on the proper procedures at each hand sink. Inspectors noted a language barrier was present and directed the person in charge to train staff to use a paper towel to shut off the water valve and avoid re-contamination after washing. "Correction of all improper hand-washing procedures was not attainable during inspection," health officials said in the report, noting they would return to observe proper hand-washing procedures. Inspectors observed an employee at the grill station grab raw products from the grill drawers with gloved hands, then proceed to place raw product on the grill and change gloves without washing their hands. An employee was also observed grabbing two heaping handfuls of dripping, raw chicken and placing it on the grill surface, splattering raw chicken juice on raw beef and raw shrimp in separate grill drawers. All shrimp and beef contaminated from this incident, about 80 pounds, was embargoed, the report said. Inspectors advised employees to place plates with tongs or large spoons between the tops of each grill drawer and bottom of the grill surface to prevent contamination and reduce the number of times staff change their gloves and wash their hands. According to the report, the person in charge advised the Environmental Health Specialist the hand sink near the dish pit was being used as a fill sink while another employee was observed using a separate hand sink as a dump sink for the sanitizer bucket. Inspectors noted the back-line hand sink was inoperable during the inspection and required a follow-up to observe it had been fixed. Two molded peppers from a bulk pepper stock and a can with a heavy dent to the hermetic seal were embargoed due to their condition, about a half pound and six pounds respectively. Inspectors observed a box of raw chicken stored over raw beef in covered, plastic buckets on metal wire shelves. Soda dispenser nozzles showed heavy debris buildup which flaked off when attempting to remove the nozzles, prompting a follow-up to observe regular cleaning, according to the report. Inspectors noted the thermometer was missing from a white, reach-in cooler where portioned salsas were stored and uncovered taco bowls and tortilla chips were found on the line. Wet, used wiping cloths were stored outside of a sanitizing solution and an employee was seen stacking wet equipment. Inspectors watched as an employee washed their gloves and documented an employee beverage stored over restaurant products in a white, reach-in cooler and an employee phone stored on metal wire shelves over clean equipment. Zero parts per million chlorine was found in the sanitizer bucket and corrected during the inspection. Health officials said a heavy gray water leak was spotted from a hand sink basin near the dish pit, requiring maintenance. The report also noted pooling water on the floors was tracked throughout the kitchen as well as kitchen floor damage.
Date of follow-up inspection: May 8
Follow-up score: 90
Address: 2524 Hwy 49 Suite A, Pleasant View
See the full inspection report
Front Porch Score: 71
Date of inspection: April 27
Examples of violations: Multiple critical items were reviewed with the person in charge during the inspection, health officials said in the report. Issues discussed included how both hand sinks were improperly stocked, and inspectors did not observe employees wash their hands, paper towels were reportedly missing at hand sinks near the dishwasher and kitchen and the dishwasher not sanitizing correctly. Proper hand-washing education was provided to the person in charge and inspectors noted a follow-up would be required within 10 days to assess correct stocking at hand sinks and the dishwasher sanitizing function. Many items in the walk-in cooler cooked the previous day were missing date marks, rags were left on tables throughout the kitchen and boxes of single use items were stored on the floor. Cutting boards and plastic utensils in the kitchen were found with deep grooves and other damage and should be replaced, inspectors noted in the report. Inspectors observed dirt and grease buildup on facility equipment and a black substance was found on walk-in cooler shelves and walls. Hot water was not available at the kitchen hand sink and damage was visible on the ceilings, floors and walls of the kitchen.
Date of follow-up inspection: May 7
Follow-up score: 93
Address: 108 Center Ave, Dickson
See the full inspection report
Guadalajara Mexican Grill Score: 77
Date of inspection: April 21
Examples of violations: Inspectors observed an employee cutting a lime with their bare hands and embargoed it during the inspection. Education was provided on ready-to-eat foods and proper glove procedure. Raw beef was found in a covered container and stored over uncovered mushrooms in prep unit one on metal wire shelves. It was moved to a better location in the prep unit, though inspectors noted the unit has limited space on the upper shelves to store non-raw products and needs smaller storage containers. Queso measuring 120-140 degrees Fahrenheit in the steam well after reheating for one and a half hours was stored in steam wells holding at 176 degrees and at risk of not meeting reheating temperatures of 165 degrees within two hours. The queso was rapidly reheated during the inspection and met and exceeded 170 degrees Fahrenheit before being returned to the steam wells. Inspectors noted a properly stored spray bottle was unlabeled, personal foods were stored in a glass reach-in cooler over restaurant products and spatulas were stored in the gap between a three-compartment sink and wall. An employee water bottle was initially observed on preparation surfaces but was moved during the inspection to a dry stock shelf with single use service items. And wiping cloths stored in sanitizer buckets with zero parts per million of chlorine present were advised to be stored in 50-100 ppm chlorine to remain in compliance.
Date of follow-up inspection: April 21
Follow-up score: 96
Address: 262 Village Square, Pleasant View
See the full inspection report
Swezey's Score: 79
Date of inspection: April 20
Examples of violations: Inspectors observed an employee wash their hands, pick up an object from the floor, dispose of an object, then motion to put on gloves for food preparation without washing their hands after contamination occurred. The employee was directed to wash their hands before putting on the gloves. An employee was then observed using a hand sink as a fill sink, even though hand sinks are exclusively used for hand washing. Education was provided to the employee. During the inspection, health officials embargoed about two pounds of kielbasa after finding reduced oxygen packaging used for the food product. The establishment was directed to cease the use of vacuum sealing and education was provided, noting "vacuum sealing can only be done with variance and/or HACCP plan in place." The person in charge elected to use food grade bags for portioning, inspectors said in the report. Inspectors noted a covered container of raw burger stored over a covered container of tomatoes on the bottom shelf of a walk-in cooler with metal wire shelving. The tomatoes were moved to a higher shelf during the inspection. Two pans of cheese sauce measured 129 and 130 degrees Fahrenheit after reheating for an hour and a half while stored in steam wells holding at 170 degrees. Inspectors noted the cheese sauces were at risk of not meeting the required reheating temperature of 165 degrees within two hours and directed both pans of cheese sauce to be reheated to at least 165 degrees during the inspection and returned to the steam wells.
Date of follow-up inspection: April 20
Follow-up score: 100
Address: 254 Village Square Suite 100, Pleasant View
See the full inspection report
Los Rancheros Score: 77
Date of inspection: April 10
Examples of violations: Inspectors said they spoke with the person in charge concerning "multiple critical items" in the report. Issues cited in the report included inspectors observing an employee washing dishes, loading dirty dishes and then putting away clean dishes without washing their hands between tasks and another employee washing their hands in the three-compartment sink. Education on proper handwashing was provided to the person in charge, though inspectors noted a follow-up would be required within 10 days. The dishwasher was not sanitizing correctly during the inspection. Date markings were not observed on any cooked items in the restaurant, prompting another follow-up. Inspectors reported damages and dirt buildup to the kitchen ceilings, floors and walls, damage to the walk-in cooler floors and walls and grease and dirt buildup on equipment. The report also noted a cutting board in the kitchen had damage and "should be sanded or replaced."
Date of follow-up inspection: April 20
Follow-up score: 97
Address: 2101 Hwy 96, Burns
See the full inspection report
Sidelines Grill Score: 67
Date of inspection: April 1
Examples of violations: Health officials said they would return within 10 days for a follow-up inspection on all critical violations and will be requesting a "permit revocation warning due to repeat critical violations." Inspectors discussed a risk control plan and noted they would provide applicable fact sheets to employees. During the inspection, health officials noted the menu lists catfish, however the kitchen was serving Swai. Inspectors directed employees to hold any orders placed on Swai until the menu has been corrected to accurately reflect what is being served, saying "if an establishment is offering catfish on the menu, it must be American catfish." Inspectors said they observed an employee enter the kitchen and begin scooping food out of the prep unit without washing their hands, according to the report. Multiple employees were also observed washing their hands at the hand sink and turning off the faucet with bare, clean hands before grabbing paper towels. Education on proper handwashing times and procedures was provided to employees. Chicken cooked on a flat top measured 160 degrees Fahrenheit when plated for service. It was placed back on the flat top to continue cooking and read 183 degrees when re-plated. Au jus and cooked chicken held hot on different stove tops that had been turned off were made three and a half hours prior and measured at 117 degree and 109 degrees respectively. Inspectors embargoed both, about 10 pounds. Several foods held cold in the walk-in cooler read between 43-49 degrees Fahrenheit, including Alfredo made on Mar. 30 stored near the front of the cooler at 49 degrees and roast beef and raw steak stored near the front/middle of the cooler at 44 degrees. About two pounds of Alfredo was embargoed and inspectors advised the person in charge to utilize ice bags or ice baths to cool foods. Inspectors noticed the brunch menu offered steak and eggs that can be ordered undercooked with no consumer advisory at the point of sale and provided guidance documents to employees. Also noted in the report, inspectors found containers of food at a steam table near the exit and numerous food items in the reach-in cooler uncovered and not protected from environmental contamination. Plastic condiment cups were seen used as scoops in croutons and other food in the prep unit. Dust buildup was found on fan covers in the walk-in cooler and the walk-in cooler condenser was observed leaking on the floor of the cooler. Inspectors reported 200 parts per million of chlorine was detected in sanitizer buckets with wiping cloths. The buckets were diluted to 100 ppm during the inspection. An employee bag was also found on the counter next to bowls and the steam table and an employee water bottle was discovered on a prep table used for breaking chicken.
Date of follow-up inspection: April 10
Follow-up score: 96
Address: 232 Hutton Place Suite 102, Ashland City
See the full inspection report
Katie Nixon can be reached at knixon@gannett.com.
This article originally appeared on Nashville Tennessean: Worst food inspections west of Nashville: Permit revocation warning sought
